title: Can you spot the rule in each of the ten rows?
description: Ten rows of numbers each follow a rule. The video says every rule in plain words and checks one of them.
teaching_notes: One idea: every row, even the row of ones, follows a rule that can be said in words. Watch for students who think a row that does not change has no pattern.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (Math Talk), p.3
video_script.why: The child states the rule of each of ten sequences in words: ones, counting, odd, even, triangular, squares, cubes, {{NAME_1}} numbers, powers of two and powers of three.
video_script.substitution: Look at how each number comes from the one before, and say it in words.
video_script.anchor: the ten rows of number sequences from the book, stacked one under the other
video_script.payoff_line: Every one of the ten rows follows a rule

final_answer.value: ones: every term is 1; counting: add 1; odd: add 2 from 1; even: add 2 from 2; triangular: add 2, 3, 4, 5; squares and cubes: multiply a number by itself; the sum of the two before; powers of 2: multiply by 2; powers of 3: multiply by 3
final_answer.spoken: every row has a rule, and each rule can be said in words

names.{{NAME_1}}: ancient Indian scholar after whom the sequence 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... is named

hold_back: Every one of the ten rows follows a rule
never_show: the row of all ones has no pattern
maths_rules: odd numbers: start at 1 and add 2 each time
even numbers: start at 2 and add 2 each time
squares: 1 x 1, 2 x 2, 3 x 3 and so on; cubes: 1 x 1 x 1, 2 x 2 x 2 and so on
{{NAME_1}} numbers: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8; each term is the sum of the two terms before it
powers of 2: multiply the last term by 2; powers of 3: multiply the last term by 3
video_script.design: One idea: every row follows a rule that can be said in words. Callback to finding a jump between neighbours. Wrong idea: a row that does not change has no pattern. The ten rows stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; ten rows of numbers stacked one under the other, each row ending in dots

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.rows: the ten rows appear one by one
marks.ask: the words the rule of each row appear beside the rows

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about ten rows of numbers.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Each row has its own pattern.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you say the rule for every one of them?

beats.on_screen: the ten rows hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one row with an arrow from each term to the next, labelled how does each come from the one before

marks.arrows: an arrow joins each term of one row to the next
marks.ask: the words how does each come from the one before appear

narration: <bookmark mark='arrows'/>Earlier we found the jump between neighbouring terms.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>To say a rule in words, we ask how each term comes from the one before.

marks.given: the starts of the ten rows are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the ten rows of numbers from your book.

beats.on_screen: To find: the rule of each row, in words

marks.find: the words the rule of each row are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the rule of each row, and say it in words.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: ones: every term is 1. Counting: add 1. Odd: start at 1, add 2. Even: start at 2, add 2

marks.ones: the first two rules are written beside their rows
marks.odd: the odd and even rules are written beside their rows

narration: <bookmark mark='ones'/>Step one, the first four rows. In the row of ones, every term is one. The counting numbers add one each time.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>The odd numbers start at one and add two each time. The even numbers start at two and add two each time.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: triangular: add 2, then 3, then 4, then 5. Squares: 1 x 1, 2 x 2, 3 x 3. Cubes: 1 x 1 x 1, 2 x 2 x 2

marks.tri: the triangular rule is written beside its row
marks.sq: the rules for squares and cubes are written beside their rows

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, the next three rows. The triangular numbers add two, then three, then four, then five, and so on.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>The squares multiply a number by itself, like two times two. The cubes multiply a number by itself three times, like two times two times two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the row named after {{NAME_1}}: each term is the sum of the two before it. Powers of 2: multiply by 2. Powers of 3: multiply by 3

marks.vira: the rule for the row named after {{NAME_1}} is written beside its row
marks.pow: the rules for powers of 2 and powers of 3 are written beside their rows

narration: <bookmark mark='vira'/>Step three, the last three rows. The numbers named after {{NAME_1}} start one, two, three, five, eight. Each is the sum of the two before it.
<bookmark mark='pow'/>The powers of two multiply the last term by two. The powers of three multiply the last term by three.

beats.on_screen: Check, the triangular row: the jumps are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 21 + 7 = 28

marks.check: the triangular row is written with its jumps

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check one row against its rule. In the triangular row, the jumps are two, three, four, five, six and seven.
<bookmark mark='fits'/>Twenty one plus seven is twenty eight, so the rule fits.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Every one of the ten rows follows a rule
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Every one of the ten rows follows a rule, and each rule can be said in words.
